card: Throws an exception in ScriptCompression::Unser when DecompressScript fails instead of silently leaving the script empty. Previously, deserialization ignored decompression failure, which in corrupt database or stream states could turn an unspendable off-curve P2PK script into an anyone-can-spend empty script without alerting calling code. The PR also marks script compression and decompression functions as nodiscard and adds test coverage for unspendable off-curve pubkeys and invalid-Y coordinates. No dependencies are noted.
evidence: PR description and commit 5500521f8b: "`ScriptCompression::Unser` ignores the `DecompressScript` return value and leaves the script empty on failure, without notifying upper layers about the error. In the worst-case scenario, which is currently only reachable through corruption, an unspendable off-curve P2PK turns into an anyone-can-spend empty script."
problem: `ScriptCompression::Unser` ignores the return value of `DecompressScript`. When decompression fails (reachable via data corruption), it leaves the script empty without throwing an error, causing what should be an unspendable script (such as an off-curve P2PK) to silently turn into an anyone-can-spend empty script.
scope_notes: A small core change in compressor.h accompanied by unit test and fuzz test additions.
summary: Throws a serialization error in `ScriptCompression::Unser` when `DecompressScript` fails instead of silently ignoring the failure. Also adds `[[nodiscard]]` to the script compression helpers and expands unit tests and fuzzing for off-curve and invalid-pubkey script decompression.
